title: The Berkeley Puzzle
question: In 1973 Berkeley admitted men at higher rates overall, yet most departments admitted women at equal or higher rates. What differed between applicant pools?
correctExplanation: Department choice — women applied disproportionately to fiercely competitive departments. Aggregates accused; strata acquitted.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is department choice. Overall rates blended easy and brutal departments unequally across genders: women crowded tough gates. Splitting by department dissolved the apparent bias.
lessonContent:
Blends accuse; strata acquit routinely.
Applicant pools differ before decisions do.
Competitive gates attract unevenly always.
Split before sentencing any institution.
Share this: split one alarming aggregate.

title: The Flipping Trend
question: A treatment looks better pooled but worse within every subgroup — or vice versa. When data are properly stratified, what typically happens to the pooled trend?
correctExplanation: It reverses — Simpson's signature: pooled trends flip under stratification. Wholes mislead where parts inform.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is it reverses. Pooling weights subgroups by size, letting big easy groups dominate: splitting restores honest comparisons. Reversal is the paradox's calling card.
lessonContent:
Pooling weights subgroups silently always.
Big easy groups dominate pooled verdicts.
Splitting restores honest comparisons.
Reversal signatures mark Simpson cases.
Share this: flip one pooled trend.

title: The Stone Sizes
question: Open surgery beat keyhole surgery overall for kidney stones, yet keyhole won for both small AND large stones separately. What hidden factor assigned treatments?
correctExplanation: Stone size — severe cases got open surgery, mild got keyhole: severity confounded the comparison. Treatments track prognoses, biasing pooled rates.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is stone size. Doctors routed big stones to open surgery and small to keyhole, so pooled rates compared prognoses, not procedures. Stratify by severity and keyhole wins twice.
lessonContent:
Doctors route by prognosis always.
Treatments track severities, biasing pools.
Pooled rates compare patients, not procedures.
Stratify before ranking treatments.
Share this: stratify one medical claim.

title: The Batting Paradox
question: Across two seasons a rival out-hit Jeter each single year, yet Jeter's combined average stood higher. What arithmetic quirk explains it?
correctExplanation: Unequal at-bats — Jeter's many at-bats came in his better year, weighting his average upward. Denominators differ, so means mislead.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is unequal at-bats. Yearly rates weighted by unequal denominators combine paradoxically: Jeter's bulk year was his best. Averages of averages lie when denominators differ.
lessonContent:
Denominators differ, so means mislead.
Bulk years weight averages silently.
Averages of averages lie routinely.
Weight rates before comparing hitters.
Share this: weight one average honestly.

title: The Age Divide
question: Country A shows higher overall fatality than Country B, yet B is deadlier within every single age group. What demographic fact resolves this?
correctExplanation: Age structure — A's older population dies more at every rate held equal. Crude rates blend demography with danger.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is age structure. Older populations die more whatever the disease does: pooled fatality confounds demography with lethality. Age-standardize before ranking nations.
lessonContent:
Demography confounds lethality in crude rates.
Older populations die more at equal danger.
Standardize ages before ranking nations.
Blends accuse; strata explain.
Share this: age-adjust one ranking.

title: The Surgeon's Load
question: The busiest surgeons post the worst mortality figures. Before concluding they are the worst surgeons, what alternative explains the ranking?
correctExplanation: Toughest cases — referrals concentrate hopeless cases on expert hands. Mortality ranks case-mix before skill.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is toughest cases. The best attract the dying: pooled mortality punishes referral centers for their courage. Risk-adjust before ranking scalpels.
lessonContent:
Referrals concentrate hopeless cases upward.
Pooled mortality punishes courage directly.
Risk-adjust before ranking any surgeons.
Case-mix precedes skill in ledgers.

title: The On-Time Illusion
question: Airline A beats Airline B overall for punctuality, yet B wins at every airport they both serve. What differs between their networks?
correctExplanation: Route distribution — A flies storm-proof hubs, B flies delay-prone ones: networks, not operations, decide pooled ranks. Compare shared airports only.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is route distribution. Overall punctuality blends easy and brutal airports unequally: A dodges storms geographically. Shared-airport comparisons reverse the headline.
lessonContent:
Geography decides pooled punctuality.
Networks, not operations, rank airlines.
Storm-proof hubs flatter overall rates.
Compare shared airports exclusively.

title: The Pay Puzzle
question: A firm pays women less on average, yet every single role pays genders equally. What structural fact explains the gap?
correctExplanation: Role segregation — women cluster in lower-paid roles: equal pay within roles, unequal distribution across them. Gaps live in assignment, not wages.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is role segregation. Within-role equality coexists with aggregate gaps when hiring sorts genders into pay bands. Discrimination moved upstream from paychecks to placements.
lessonContent:
Assignment gaps precede paycheck gaps.
Sorting explains what wages cannot.
Within-role equality hides across-role skew.
Upstream discrimination flows downstream.

title: The Hospital Link
question: Two unrelated diseases appear strongly linked in hospital records though independent in the population. What selection effect manufactures the link?
correctExplanation: Admission bias — hospitals oversample the doubly ill: either disease raises admission odds, so wards concentrate coincidences. Berkson's paradox in white coats.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is admission bias. Population independence means nothing after admission filters: having either condition boosts hospitalization, stacking wards with both. Samples select; selections mislead.
lessonContent:
Admission filters manufacture false links.
Wards concentrate coincidences systematically.
Population truths die at hospital doors.
Samples select before statistics speak.
Share this: suspect one selected sample.

title: The Smoker Babies
question: Among low-birth-weight infants, babies of smokers paradoxically survive better than those of non-smokers. What statistical artifact explains this?
correctExplanation: Collider bias — conditioning on low birth weight (caused by smoking AND other worse causes) selects hardy smokers' babies against tragic others'. Stratifying on consequences corrupts causes.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is collider bias. Low birth weight has many parents: smoking (mild) versus anomalies (severe). Conditioning on the shared consequence compares mild-cause babies against severe-cause ones. Colliders corrupt comparisons.
lessonContent:
Shared consequences corrupt cause comparisons.
Conditioning on effects biases causes.
Mild-cause babies beat severe-cause ones.
Colliders punish naive stratification.
Share this: uncondition one collider.

title: The Exposed Staff
question: Vaccinated hospital workers show higher crude infection rates than the unvaccinated public. Before doubting vaccines, what differs between the groups?
correctExplanation: Greater exposure — wards bathe staff in virus: crude rates compare exposure, not efficacy. Stratify by contact intensity first.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is greater exposure. Hospital air differs from home air enormously: pooled comparisons punish the protected-exposed. Efficacy lives in matched strata, never crude pools.
lessonContent:
Wards bathe staff in extra virus.
Crude rates compare exposures, not efficacies.
Matched strata reveal true protection.
Pools punish the protected-exposed.
Share this: match one comparison fairly.

title: The Pooling Question
question: Analysts ask whether to trust pooled or split figures. Statisticians answer: consult the causal structure first. What ultimately decides?
correctExplanation: Causal structure — graphs dictate adjusting for confounders, never mediators or colliders. Method follows metaphysics here.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is causal structure. Pool-or-split has no statistical answer: only causal graphs say which variables contaminate and which carry effects. Draw first, average second.
lessonContent:
Graphs dictate pooling decisions entirely.
Metaphysics precedes methodology here.
Draw causes before averaging effects.
Structure decides; data merely obeys.
Share this: draw one causal graph.

title: The Hidden Path
question: Exercise protects hearts partly through weight loss. Adjusting for weight erases most of exercise's apparent benefit. What was wrongly adjusted away?
correctExplanation: The mediator — weight carries exercise's effect: controlling for it blocks the very pathway studied. Adjust away mechanisms and nothing remains.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is the mediator. Confounders demand adjustment; mediators forbid it: weight transmits exercise's benefit downstream. Controlling pathways erases the effects they carry.
lessonContent:
Pathways carry effects downstream always.
Controlling mediators erases findings.
Confounders adjust; mediators transmit.
Distinguish blockers from carriers.
Share this: spare one mediator.

title: The Dissolving Gap
question: Every aggregate disparity dissolves upon finding the stratified mechanism behind it. What single discovery resolves all Simpson cases?
correctExplanation: The confounder — every reversal surrenders to a found third variable: departments, severity, age. Find it and paradoxes evaporate.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is the confounder. Aggregates accuse until strata explain: departments, stones, ages — each paradox kept one hidden variable. Discovery dissolves disparity mechanically.
lessonContent:
Hidden variables author apparent paradoxes.
Discovery dissolves disparities mechanically.
Third variables explain first impressions.
Find confounders before crying foul.

title: The Lying Numbers
question: Pundits cite Simpson's paradox to claim statistics generally deceive and all data work is futile. Does the paradox prove numbers lie?
correctExplanation: No — Simpson's proves stratification matters, not that numbers lie. Properly split data tell truth reliably.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is no. The paradox indicts pooling, never statistics: stratified analyses behave impeccably. Cynicism misreads a method lesson as nihilism.
lessonContent:
Pooling indicted; statistics acquitted fully.
Stratified analyses behave impeccably.
Method lessons differ from nihilism.
Cynicism misreads precision's demands.
Share this: defend one honest number.

title: The Patient's Rate
question: A small-stone patient asks which surgery success rate applies to her: the pooled figures or the small-stone figures. Which should she use?
correctExplanation: Their subgroup rate — patients belong to strata, never pools: small-stone figures predict small-stone outcomes. Reference classes must match.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is their subgroup rate. Pooled numbers blend strangers' prognoses: relevance demands matching reference classes. Patients are subgroups walking, not populations averaged.
lessonContent:
Reference classes must match patients.
Pools blend strangers' prognoses uselessly.
Subgroups predict their members best.
Belonging beats averaging for decisions.

title: The League Illusion
question: Raw school league tables rank wealthy-suburb schools far above inner-city ones. What intake fact confounds the comparison?
correctExplanation: Student intake — schools inherit results through admissions: raw tables rank intakes, not teaching. Value-added adjusts; raw misleads.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is student intake. League tables compare starting lines disguised as finish lines: privileged intakes guarantee ranked outputs. Teaching quality hides behind enrollment.
lessonContent:
Starting lines disguise as finishes routinely.
Intakes guarantee ranked outputs largely.
Value-added adjusts; raw misleads.
Teaching hides behind enrollment always.

title: The Gilded Ranking
question: Elite universities top outcome rankings partly because they admit the already-advantaged. What resource confounds prestige with performance?
correctExplanation: Incoming wealth — selective gates admit resources, then claim credit for outcomes. Rankings launder privilege into prestige.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is incoming wealth. Outcomes follow inputs more than instruction: admitting advantage manufactures ranked success. Prestige maps admissions, never alchemy.
lessonContent:
Gates admit resources, then claim credit.
Rankings launder privilege into prestige.
Outcomes follow inputs more than teaching.
Selectivity manufactures ranked success.

title: The Discrimination Test
question: Aggregate gaps alone cannot prove discrimination — nor disprove it. What must claims examine beyond pooled figures?
correctExplanation: Subgroup comparisons — justice needs strata: pooled gaps allege, stratified gaps convict or acquit. Fairness audits split first.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is subgroup comparisons. Aggregates alone prove nothing either way: Berkeley acquitted, other cases convict — strata decide. Split data before judging institutions.
lessonContent:
Strata convict or acquit fairly.
Aggregates allege; splits decide.
Fairness audits stratify first always.
Pooled gaps prove nothing alone.
Share this: split one fairness claim.

title: The State Mirage
question: US states with more immigrants show higher literacy — yet immigrants individually test lower. Group correlations reversing at individual level have a name. What is it?
correctExplanation: Ecological fallacy — Robinson (1950): state patterns need not hold for persons. Groups differ from members systematically.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is ecological fallacy. Literate states attract striving immigrants: group truth inverts individual truth. Persons are not precincts, ever.
lessonContent:
Persons are not precincts, ever.
Group truths invert individual ones.
States attract what individuals lack.
Aggregate patterns mislead members.
Share this: unmix one group claim.

title: The Staged Miracle
question: When cancer staging improved, survival rose in EVERY stage without any treatment advance — sicker patients simply got reclassified upward. What caused the miracle?
correctExplanation: Stage migration — the Will Rogers effect: moving the sickest 'early' patients to 'late' raises both groups' averages. Reclassification manufactures progress.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is stage migration. Better scans re-sorted patients: early stages shed their worst, late stages gained their best — both averages rose, nobody lived longer. Definitions cured no one.
lessonContent:
Reclassification manufactures progress illusions.
Definitions cure no one, ever.
Averages rise while lives don't.
Staging changes rewrite histories falsely.
Share this: spot one staged miracle.

title: The Golden Shuffle
question: Observational studies drown in hidden confounders, yet randomized trials mostly escape Simpson's trap. What protects them?
correctExplanation: Randomization — shuffling balances known and unknown confounders across arms. Chance deals fair strata automatically.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is randomization. Random assignment equalizes everything in expectation: measured and unmeasured confounders split evenly. Shuffles manufacture fairness mechanically.
lessonContent:
Shuffles manufacture fairness mechanically.
Chance balances unknown confounders.
Expectation equalizes all arms eventually.
Randomize before trusting comparisons.
Share this: shuffle one comparison fairly.

title: The Drawn Causes
question: Modern analysts map variables as nodes and arrows before deciding what to adjust for. What diagrams guide pooling choices?
correctExplanation: Causal diagrams — DAGs mark confounders (adjust), mediators and colliders (don't). Pictures precede pooling decisions.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is causal diagrams. Nodes and arrows encode adjustment rules visually: block backdoors, spare frontdoors, never condition colliders. Draw first, average second.
lessonContent:
Pictures precede pooling decisions.
Backdoors block; frontdoors flow.
Colliders never condition, ever.
Draw causes before averaging effects.

title: The Averaged Average
question: Analysts average two hospitals' rates (80% and 60%) to get 70% — but unequal patient counts make this wrong. What invalidates averaging averages?
correctExplanation: Unequal denominators — means need weighting by size: 80% of 100 plus 60% of 900 is 62%, not 70%. Denominators decide, never numerators alone.
incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is unequal denominators. Unweighted means assume equal groups falsely: weight by patients or perish. Denominators rule every average of averages.
lessonContent:
Weight by size or perish statistically.
Unweighted means assume falsely always.
Denominators rule average-of-averages.
Numerators alone decide nothing.
Share this: weight one average properly.

title: The Split Display
question: Tables hide reversals that pictures reveal: plotting each subgroup separately exposes what pooled numbers conceal. What display catches Simpson cases?
correctExplanation: Split plots — faceted displays let each subgroup tell its truth: reversals surface visually. Pictures precede paradoxes.
incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is split plots. Stratified charts expose what pooled tables bury: eyes catch reversals arithmetic hides. Visualize splits before trusting pools.
lessonContent:
Eyes catch what tables bury.
Facets let subgroups testify truly.
Visualize splits before trusting pools.
Pictures precede paradox detection.
